# YumCSS performance details

For the concise real-world comparison, see [PERF-SUMMARY.md](PERF-SUMMARY.md). This detailed report includes committed typecheck, runtime-throughput, bundle-size, generated Tailwind metadata, CSS-in-JS Bench, and Arena snapshots. Lower is better for typecheck/size; higher is better for throughput. Rankings are per workload and metric, not a universal library score.

TypeScript measurements use fresh processes and the pinned TypeScript version in each benchmark. Runtime-throughput measurements are local in-process calls. Runtime-size measurements are minified browser bundles with gzip level 6.

### Targeted runtime optimization follow-up

Measured on darwin/arm64 with Node v24.20.0 on 2026-09-25. Each process median is based on five in-process samples of two million calls, from the isolated Vitest runtime API benchmark. This targeted follow-up is separate from the pinned all-API ranking snapshot.

| API         | Operation                                                                    |                 Before median ops/s (run range) |                  After median ops/s (run range) | Change |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------: | ----------------------------------------------: | -----: |
| stack.style | renderer-agnostic Stack style mapping for direction=row, gap=4, align=center | 13,670,556 (11,774,007–13,693,456; 3 processes) | 20,084,136 (20,061,530–20,084,136; 2 processes) | +46.9% |

The recorded within-process P10–P90 envelope was 8,822,551–13,245,804 ops/s before (one run retained percentiles) and 19,562,684–20,178,843 ops/s after. Source revisions: before 41a909fa9560c1cdd983f998329bf3602b277ccb; after d1b6fc227d9a984c5b86f030cdd151331a22e360. This focused runtime result does not establish a full application build win or a cross-library rank change; the all-API table above remains pinned to its recorded snapshot.

Measured 2026-09-25 on Apple M4 (arm64), macOS with Node 24.20.0, Tailwind CSS 4.3.3, TypeScript 7.0.2, and Vite 8.2.2. Before YumCSS revision 5a4797777994da5ba93f5b9ffeacc1059c6b64a9; after change xlqxnyqlywumvszkwwowypxznqorynlt.

The official default-only codegen produced 414 utilities and 88 variants. Its declaration was 134,434 raw bytes; the customized Playground declaration was 142,978 bytes. The stock interop artifact was 723,737 raw / 35,581 gzip bytes. The measured YumCSS package tarball was 338,079 bytes.

The shared default-catalog design remains a no-go: measurements do not show a lower combined package, generated-project, and TypeScript cost, and no shared type export was added. The compiler continues to load the effective project catalog through the official Tailwind loader.

| Measurement                            |      Before |       After |             Change |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------: | ----------: | -----------------: |
| All generated project artifacts (raw)  | 1,248,282 B | 1,015,391 B |         -232,891 B |
| Self-contained interop artifact (raw)  |   781,244 B |   548,353 B | -232,891 B (29.8%) |
| Self-contained interop artifact (gzip) |    43,563 B |    39,537 B |    -4,026 B (9.2%) |
| Playground MigrationLabPage (raw)      |   536,967 B |   431,679 B | -105,288 B (19.6%) |
| Playground MigrationLabPage (gzip)     |    52,058 B |    48,176 B |    -3,882 B (7.5%) |

Historical prototype measurement: this compared yumcss.interop/1 to yumcss.interop/2 before publication. The prototype stored each generated value union once by type alias and kept utility rows as references. The current pre-launch artifact is flattened to the single yumcss.interop/1 schema, with no token sub-schema or compatibility reader. Node zlib gzipSync default level on Node 24.20.0. The then-after bundle was verified to contain the measured prototype schema and generated utility values (both present).

TypeScript diagnostics were 340,769 instantiations; 467,842 KiB; 0.462 s check before and 340,499 instantiations; 465,901 KiB; 0.604 s check after. The after run includes one additional test file and its check time is not lower; this is not a typecheck-performance claim.

The full pnpm --filter playground run tw:generate command measured median 5.00 s, range 4.71–5.26 s (5.26, 4.71, 5.00) before and median 3.64 s, range 3.36–4.06 s (3.64, 4.06, 3.36) after, with peak process RSS 124.4, 124.2, 125.2 MiB before and 124.0, 123.3, 123.4 MiB after. Includes pnpm, codegen CLI, oxfmt, and generated manifest refresh. These samples support the size result but do not isolate generator CPU time.

The CSS-in-JS Bench and Arena rankings are unchanged: this is a Playground migration-tool chunk, not a benchmarked styling lane. The static and dynamic tw() runtime paths, conflict metadata, and generated APIs remain intact.

Normalized evidence: [snapshot.json](benchmarks/tw-codegen/snapshot.json).

## CSS-in-JS Bench detailed results

WPD 0.15.1 completed 2026-09-26T08:49:49.145Z on Apple M4 (arm64) with Node v24.20.0, Chrome 154.0.8037.57, and Firefox stable_156.0.1. CSS-in-JS Bench revision 3f8df1511738; YumCSS artifact revision 9a9f9c499e7f43f8b05811634613a2d2419fe156; 21 lanes and 13 workload definitions. The CSS lane is the 400-tile product-grid case. Rankings compare yumcss-css with non-YumCSS peer lanes; per-call JS, CSS, and SSR HTML payload components are gzip bytes. Browser measurements are Chrome medians.

### Primary `createCss` lane

The lane uses `createCss(preset)`, static `css.class(...)` declarations, and a multi-map `css(...)` plus `css.props(...)` host boundary through the shipped `yumcssExtractVite(css)` plugin. Only the rating percentage remains a runtime style value.
The CSS-in-JS Bench page does not call `cx()`, so it does not exercise the class-map compiler optimization. The current YumCSS SSR median reports a 33.7% spread. Its rank measures this fixture; it is not evidence for or against the `cx()` change.

The 800-style Brotli growth, after subtracting each engine's zero-style output, was:

| Engine / strategy  | Brotli growth per declaration |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Bamboo             | 2.18 B / declaration          |
| StyleX             | 5.95 B / declaration          |
| Panda              | 2.14 B / declaration          |
| YumCSS hash        | 6.30 B / declaration          |
| YumCSS named atoms | 2.01 B / declaration          |

The default hash lane adds 30,244 Brotli bytes across 4,800 unique declarations (6.30 B per declaration). Its raw increase is accounted for exactly by class names, selector syntax, declaration text, rule syntax, and line separation below. These raw categories are additive; Brotli and gzip are not, so their growth is measured on complete emitted assets.

| Raw CSS component     |  Bytes |
| --------------------- | -----: |
| Class-name characters | 10,753 |
| Other selector syntax | 34,158 |
| Declaration text      | 90,500 |
| Rule syntax           |  9,600 |
| Inter-rule whitespace |  4,800 |

The added rules stay in the existing @layer utilities context. They add 0 conditional wrappers and 0 layer-wrapper bytes.

Named atoms lower the synthetic 800-style CSS slope from 6.30 to 2.01 Brotli bytes per declaration; their 17,763 B output edges Bamboo's 17,833 B by 70 B at this volume. The strict experimental ≤2.00 B/declaration assertion exits nonzero at the measured 2.014 B/declaration (displayed as 2.0). On the ordinary 400-tile Bench page, named atoms raise transfer from 10,539 B to 18,352 B gzip and add 89,501 raw class-attribute bytes across Arena routes. Keep hash classes as the default.

## Real-world Vite extraction: Emisoup and Playground

Measured 2026-09-25 on Apple M4 (arm64), macOS, Node 24.20.0, Vite 8.3.0. Emisoup source 005b44b87470228738873fd66076737a2017b3; YumCSS before scan gate 04fe7147674974a773d958507d7b5e93c76187ef; after 94df3c41d5209e92adcadd298d0d246c37932a5a.

| Workload   | Modules | Before runs (s)  | Before median | After runs (s)   | After median |
| ---------- | ------: | ---------------- | ------------: | ---------------- | -----------: |
| Emisoup    |   3,026 | 5.45, 7.28, 9.21 |        7.28 s | 7.24, 7.07, 8.67 |       7.24 s |
| Playground |   4,220 | 6.67, 5.35, 5.61 |        5.61 s | 6.04, 5.04, 4.50 |       5.04 s |

The small full-build median shifts are within run-to-run spread and do not establish a build-time win. Two after runs measured 1.05–1.08 GB maximum resident memory. The deterministic 1,000-file source-scan workload improved from 9.70 ms median parse-and-walk to 0.275 ms median guarded discovery (35.3×). Parser calls fell from 1,000 to 0. This phase result is not a multiplier for the full application build.

The single CPU-profile pair sampled 7.529 s before and 5.705 s after; AST-walk samples fell from 1.497 s to 0.990 s (34% lower). Treat one profile per side as supporting evidence, not a repeated build-time result.

One instrumented build completed in 6.79 s. The CSS transform hook ran 3,026 times for 46.83 s cumulative inclusive time; concurrent module transforms overlap. CSS generateBundle took 2.63 s. Stack-fold transform used 0.34 s cumulative across 3,026 calls. The wrapper adds timing overhead.

### Source eligibility filtering in production bundle extraction

A production-bundle regression reproduced: an excluded bundled module contributed CSS because its ID reached CSS collection without the same include/exclude gate used during source transforms. The fix exposes `CssSourceWorkspace.isScanned(file)` as the shared eligibility check and applies it before main, split, and critical CSS collection.

Measured 2026-09-25 on Apple M4 (arm64), macOS, Node 24.20.0, with Emisoup Vite 8.3.0 and Playground Vite 8.2.2. Emisoup source a13301f9a663b2190cdfd9ac4969794b2c3d6b74; baseline YumCSS 180ceaf1a8ab011f62e1a929fbc9a2c56f3da1e1; filtered YumCSS 41a909fa9560c1cdd983f998329bf3602b277ccb.

| Workload   | Command                                  | Before full-build samples                                               | After full-build samples                                                | Before process-tree RSS                                 | After process-tree RSS                                              |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Emisoup    | `pnpm --filter @emisoup/front run build` | median 5.91 s, range 5.67–7.04 s (7.04, 5.88, 5.67, 5.91, 6.01)         | median 7.18 s, range 7.00–9.49 s (9.49, 7.84, 7.18, 7.00, 7.06)         | median 1213 MiB, range 1188–1302 MiB (1302, 1213, 1188) | median 1183 MiB, range 1140–1198 MiB (1184, 1198, 1171, 1183, 1140) |
| Playground | `pnpm --filter playground run build`     | median 12.39 s, range 11.66–17.41 s (17.41, 12.39, 11.66, 12.17, 13.21) | median 11.32 s, range 10.70–13.95 s (13.95, 11.32, 11.54, 10.70, 10.92) | median 1144 MiB, range 1090–1170 MiB (1090, 1144, 1170) | median 1197 MiB, range 1041–1213 MiB (1197, 1210, 1213, 1190, 1041) |

RSS sums pnpm and descendant processes, sampled every 75 ms. The full-process medians were 5.91 s → 7.18 s for Emisoup and 12.39 s → 11.32 s for Playground. The ranges overlap; these samples show no repeatable end-to-end build or memory win.

A separate instrumented Emisoup Vite API profile used 3 sequential builds per mode in one Node process. CSS transform ran 3,026 times per run; cumulative transform timings are inclusive and can overlap.

| Profile measure              | Filter disabled                                           | Filter enabled                                            |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Build API wall time          | median 5.97 s, range 3.68–6.94 s (6.94, 5.97, 3.68)       | median 3.65 s, range 3.29–6.44 s (6.44, 3.65, 3.29)       |
| CSS transform inclusive time | median 36.05 s, range 31.09–38.81 s (36.05, 38.81, 31.09) | median 37.37 s, range 26.32–61.95 s (61.95, 26.32, 37.37) |
| CSS generateBundle time      | median 1.88 s, range 0.94–1.99 s (1.99, 1.88, 0.94)       | median 0.84 s, range 0.83–1.46 s (1.46, 0.84, 0.83)       |

The generateBundle median fell from 1.883 s to 0.841 s (about 55%) in this warm, instrumented profile. Samples are cache-sensitive and their ranges overlap; this is targeted hook evidence, not a full-build speedup. The change fixes the excluded-source leak. Arena's current-output recheck preserves its measured metrics; the Bench ranking remains tied to its pinned measured artifact and was not rerun here.

### Emisoup client output

Files are compressed separately with Node zlib gzip level 9 and Brotli quality 11. Totals cover the HTML and all emitted JS/CSS assets, not just the initial route.

| Asset group | Files | Raw bytes | gzip 9 bytes | Brotli 11 bytes |
| ----------- | ----: | --------: | -----------: | --------------: |
| HTML        |     1 |     5,739 |        1,516 |           1,226 |
| JavaScript  |   196 | 2,872,183 |      871,079 |         771,249 |
| CSS         |     2 |   125,582 |       21,958 |          19,146 |
| Total       |   199 | 3,003,504 |      894,553 |         791,621 |

The main YumCSS stylesheet is 123,976 raw bytes, 21,169 gzip-9 bytes, and 18,496 Brotli-11 bytes. The progress-fill case emits 1 transition rule and 1 width-variable rule; the authored token path is absent from output, and runtime values 30% and 70% keep the class stable.

The stylesheet has 1,963 rules and 348 repeated declaration-body groups (862 rules, 21,654 repeated raw declaration bytes under an exact declaration-order and at-rule-context key). An order-preserving adjacent-rule prototype merged 0 rules and saved 0 raw, 0 gzip, and 0 Brotli bytes. No CSS interning change was adopted; combining non-adjacent rules could cross cascade entries.

Arena's shared JavaScript remains attributed to YumCSS runtime, preset, cx, and app modules; the measured fold changed none of the six route modules. No JavaScript was removed. Route splitting remains opt-in without first-paint and client-navigation evidence; hashed class names remain the default.

## External benchmark refresh

After refreshing CSS-in-JS Bench in a separate checkout, import its generated report with `node scripts/import-css-in-js-bench.mjs /path/to/BENCHMARK.json <yumcss-commit>`. Update the [CSS-in-JS Arena snapshot](benchmarks/css-in-js-arena/snapshot.json) only after its YumCSS lane passes the six-page parity gates; that snapshot drives the Arena rankings in PERF-SUMMARY.md.

## Sources and refresh commands

- Generated Tailwind metadata: run pnpm --filter playground run tw:generate and pnpm --filter playground run build, then update benchmarks/tw-codegen/snapshot.json
- Typecheck ecosystem: `pnpm run bench:tsc:styling -- --update`
- Generated facade comparison: `pnpm run bench:tsc:generated -- --update`
- Package/example typecheck: `pnpm run bench:tsc -- --update` and `pnpm run bench:tsc:example -- --update`
- Public API typecheck: `pnpm --filter yumcss run test:tsc -- -u`
- Runtime size: `pnpm --filter yumcss exec vitest run runtime-size -u`
- Runtime API throughput: `pnpm --filter yumcss run test:benchmarks -- -u`
- Ecosystem bundle-size comparison: `pnpm run bench:size:ecosystem -- --update`
- Real-world CSS extraction evidence: `benchmarks/real-world-css-extraction/snapshot.json`
- Summary freshness: `pnpm run bench:summary:check`
